name: Kunsthalle Recklinghausen
funding: Museen der Stadt Recklinghausen, NRW culture ministry, Kunststiftung NRW, Sparkasse Vest, Ruhrfestspiele (city and DGB union federation), Förderverein für Bildende Kunst; WDR 3 media partner.
records_note: A city museum with no report or board of its own; the city posts audited accounts, and the site shows four undated funder logos.

name: EMST National Museum of Contemporary Art
funding: Greek state €40M by 2020, plus €3M from the Stavros Niarchos Foundation (shipping).
watch: 2019 governance dispute over the director, not a funding issue.
records_note: No annual report or accounts; the footer shows undated logos for the Culture Ministry, SNF and Samsung, and the site names a nine-member administrative board.

name: NEON
funding: Private non-profit founded by collector Dimitris Daskalopoulos (food industry).
records_note: No annual report, accounts, funder list or board; the partners page names cultural partners, and the about page says only that NEON is a non-profit.

name: MOMus
funding: State museum group under the Greek Ministry of Culture.
records_note: No annual report, accounts or sponsor list found; the about page names the management board chair, vice chair, seven members and the general director.

name: Bienal de Arte Paiz
funding: 24th edition (2025-26) run by Fundación Paiz; founder money from the Paiz retail family.
records_note: Neither the Bienal nor Fundación Paiz posts a report, accounts or donor list; the foundation page names only its board president, María Regina Paiz.

name: FOKAL
funding: Open Society Foundations paid a final package in 2024 as it closed its national foundations. Kellogg, Ford and Citi-CAF fund it; the diaspora fund Ayiti Demen raised $609,068.
watch: The EU, AFD and USAID have withdrawn. Gang violence closed Martissant Park to the public.
records_note: Posts annual reports 2016 to 2024 that name funders and an external audit; the board is listed at five members. No financial statements are posted.

name: Ghetto Biennale
watch: Biennial on the Grand Rue, Port-au-Prince; Atis Rezistans also took part in documenta fifteen in 2022. No controversy found.
records_note: Its edition pages name sponsors in text for 2015, 2017 and 2019, but there are no annual reports, accounts or board list.

name: Ludwig Museum Budapest
funding: Hungarian state, with the Ludwig Foundation collection.
records_note: The museum posts narrative reports for 2005 to 2025 and budget accounts for 2011 to 2025, shows two undated logos, and names no board.

name: Reykjavík Art Museum
funding: Municipal museum funded by the City of Reykjavík.
records_note: Posts its 2023 annual report; its parent City of Reykjavik posts consolidated annual accounts. No sponsor list, and no current board for the museum.

name: Ruya Foundation
watch: KAR Group, Kurdistan's largest private oil firm (Khurmala field, refineries), is on its sponsor list; the page dates from about 2015-18.
why_flagged: KAR Group, Kurdistan's largest private oil firm (Khurmala field, refineries), is on its sponsor list; the page dates from about 2015-18.
records_note: Its About page lists sponsors and supporters, mostly as logos, undated, but posts no annual reports, accounts or board.

name: GAMeC
funding: City of Bergamo, with corporate sponsors including SABO (manufacturer).
records_note: It posts yearly accounts for 2017 to 2025 that name 27 private funders for 2025, and lists its board, but no separate annual report.

name: MAMbo
funding: Municipal museum of the City of Bologna.
records_note: The museum's own sites could not be read, so its reports, accounts, funders and board stay unchecked.
